images.alt: Behind Zach Randolph's third straight game scoring 30 points or more, the Blazers overcame the second largest first quarter deficit in NBA History. Only the New York Knicks pulled off a more impressive victory, gaining a victory vs the Los Angeles Lakers after a 27-point first quarter deficit on January 8, 1967.

Randolph, scoreless during the opening quarter, finished with 31 points, becoming the sixth Portland player to have three straight 30-point games, scoring 35 and 36 points in his two previous games.

Randolph joins Jim Paxson, Kiki Vandeweghe, and Rasheed Wallace, as each had a three game streak of over 30 points. Clyde Drexler recorded a three-game streak in three different seasons while Geoff Petrie had five such three-game streaks. In fact, Petrie also had three four-game streaks, and one streak of five games.

Drexler had one particular three game streak during the 1988/89 season of over 35-points, the only Blazers player to reach that mark to this point.
